title: emob estate
description:
The whole estate: every section any daemon reads (spec 012).

The daemons keep their own narrower views — a malformed tariff does not
stop `empd` — and this one is what `emob check` and the published JSON
Schema describe. A section no daemon reads is refused here, so
`[[subscriber]]` for `[[subscribers]]` is a refusal and not a silence.

meter_keys.description: The keys that make energy billable.

witness.description: The keys journal heads are signed under.

subscribers.description: Systems outside the estate that receive events.

operator.description:
The charge point operator: the party the stations, CDRs and invoices are
issued under.

provider.description: The e-mobility provider `empd` runs: the party its tokens are issued by.

Station.description: `[[stations]]` — one charging station and the point it is.

identity.description: The OCPP identity it connects under.

security_profile.description:
The security profile it must connect with
`[OCPP 2.0.1 Part 2 §A00]`: 1 (Basic over plain WebSocket),
2 (Basic over TLS) or 3 (TLS client certificate). There is no profile 0.

password_hash.description:
Profiles 1 and 2: its Basic password as an Argon2id PHC string
(`csmsd hash-password` prints one). A hash is not a credential, so it is
written here rather than named as an environment variable.

evse.description: The EVSE its sessions are attributed to.

rated_power_kw.description: What it can deliver, in kW — the `[AFIR Art. 5(4)]` threshold reads it.

tariff.description: The id of the `[[tariffs]]` entry that rates its sessions.

receipt_display_minutes.description:
How many minutes (1–15) the station's display shows the receipt link
after a session — `csmsd` sends it as `SetDisplayMessage`
`[OCPP 2.0.1 Part 2 §O]` (spec 011). Absent is off: a screen is public,
and the next person at it can read the link.

commissioned.description: The day it went into service, `YYYY-MM-DD` — the asset card's age.

Ocpp.description: The OCPP version a station speaks.

Location.description:
Where a station stands, as a roaming partner and the national access point
are told it. Coordinates are exact decimals: they travel as decimal text in
OCPI and DATEX II and never become a float here.

id.description: The location's id, unique per operator.

time_zone.description: The IANA zone the site's local time is read in.

MeterKey.description:
`[[meter_keys]]` — a meter's public key, out of band, with where it came
from `[OCMF §Relation of Serial Numbers]`.

gateway.description: The gateway serial (`GS`), where the key is bound to the pair.

curve.description: The curve, as `[OCMF Tab. 22]` names it (`secp256r1`, …).

key.description: The public key, hex — SEC1 or `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`.

valid_from.description: From when the key is valid (RFC 3339); unbounded when absent.

valid_until.description: Until when (RFC 3339, exclusive); unbounded when absent.

provenance.description: Where the key came from — a type approval, a cabinet reading.

time_zone.description: The IANA zone its times are read in (D175).

energy.description:
Gross price per kWh, VAT included — the figure a driver is shown
`[PAngV §3(1)]`; [`TariffSpec::vat`] is the rate inside it.

vat.description: The VAT rate inside [`TariffSpec::energy`], in percent.

Partner.description: `[[partners]]` — a provider this operator settles with.

party.description: Its party id; a contract whose issuer this is routes here.

token_a_env.description:
The variable holding the Token A handed to it out of band
`[OCPI 2.3.0 §credentials]`.

signed_data.description: Whether it requires the signed data on every CDR.

settles_within_days.description: The window it settles within, in days.

specification.description: The specification its invoices are written in.

buyer_reference.description: BT-10 — its reference for our invoices (a Leitweg-ID for a public buyer).

mandate.description: Its direct-debit mandate; without one, it pays by transfer.

EnvRef.description: The name of an environment variable that holds a secret.

Billing.description: The party details an invoice needs.

electronic_address.description:
The e-mail address an e-invoice is addressed to (BT-34 / BT-49,
scheme `EM`), which `XRechnung` requires of both parties.

InvoiceSpecification.description: The EN 16931 specification a partner's invoices are written in (BT-24).

oneOf.description: EN 16931 itself — what `[UStG §14(1)]` names for a business recipient.
`XRechnung` 3.0 — a German public buyer, or a partner that asks for it.

MandateSeed.description: A SEPA direct-debit mandate a partner signed (BT-89, BT-91).

vat_rate.description: The standard VAT rate, in percent, where the energy is supplied.

iban.description: The operator's account, paid into by transfer (BT-84).

creditor_id.description: The operator's SEPA creditor identifier (BT-90), for a mandate.

public_url.description: The origin `billd`'s invoice pages are reached at: `<public_url>/i/<token>`.

delivery.description: The operator system invoices are handed to.

InvoiceContact.description: The seller's contact on an invoice (BG-6), which `XRechnung` requires.

InvoiceDelivery.description:
`[billing.delivery]` — the operator system (ERP, Peppol provider) every
issued invoice is handed to, signed (spec 010).

url.description: Where invoices are posted: `https://`, or `http://` on loopback only.

secret_env.description: The variable holding the Standard Webhooks secret (`whsec_…`).

InvoiceSyntax.description: The syntax a delivered invoice is written in.

TokenSeed.description: One token on a seeded contract.

uid.description: The uid the card or app presents.

Operator.description: `[[operators]]` — who may read the read models.

name.description:
Who this is: the name every journal record and log line this operator
causes carries (`operator:<name>`), 1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9*._:=+|@ -]`.

token_env.description: The variable holding the bearer token.

Csms.description:
`[csms]` — how `csmsd`'s OCPP listener is exposed.

Every path is relative to the estate file (see [`Csms::path`]).

client_ca.description: The CA a profile-3 station's certificate must chain to, PEM.

tls_terminated_by_proxy.description: TLS is terminated in front of `csmsd` by a proxy the operator runs.

messages_per_minute.description: The most messages one connection may send per minute.

idle_timeout_secs.description: How long a session may stay silent before it is closed.

Desk.description:
`billd` and `roamd` are reached at their `[services]` addresses; `csmsd`'s
shell is named here because no other daemon calls it.

csmsd.description: `csmsd`'s shell base URL (its read model, not its OCPP socket).

token_env.description:
The variable holding the operator token `deskd` reads the read models
with — one of the `[[operators]]` tokens.

time_zone.description: The IANA zone the page tells the time and "today" in.

ocpp_url.description:
Where stations reach the CSMS, as an installer types it
(`wss://csms.example.com/ocpp`) — printed on the onboarding sheet.

public_url.description:
The origin a driver reaches the shell at; links are
`<public_url>/r/<token>`.

Services.description: `[services]` — where the daemons reach each other, and how.

webhook_secret_env.description: The variable holding the Standard Webhooks secret (`whsec_…`).

service_token_env.description: The variable holding the token `csmsd` presents to `empd`.

authorize_timeout_ms.description: How long `csmsd` waits for `empd` before answering `Invalid`.

retry_secs.description: How often an outbox or a roaming queue is retried.

public_url.description: Where partners reach this node's OCPI root (ending in `/ocpi`).

reach_back_allow.description:
Hosts the credentials reach-back may contact over `http` or at a
private, loopback or link-local address. Empty in production.

Witness.description:
`[desk]` — what the operator page reads, and with which token.

`[witness]` — what the witness trusts (spec 008).

`keys` names a daemon's head-verifier key (`emob/<daemon>+<8 hex>+<base64>`,
what `GET /v1/<daemon>/head` sends in `Emob-Verifier-Key`). A daemon not
named is pinned the first time the witness sees it — trust on first use,
which Heute says.

Subscriber.description:
`[[subscribers]]` — a system outside the estate that receives events.

Each event a daemon emits whose type one of `types` admits
([`crate::events::matches`]) is posted to `url` as a structured-mode
[`crate::cloudevent::CloudEvent`], signed with this subscriber's own secret,
and retried until it answers `2xx`. A subscriber added later receives what
is emitted from then on.

name.description: Its name; the journal records an answer as `subscriber:<name>`.

url.description: Where events are posted: `https://`, or `http://` on loopback only.

secret_env.description: The variable holding its Standard Webhooks secret (`whsec_…`).

types.description: The types it takes: concrete types or `*`-terminated prefixes.
